questions.question: Which method separates an insoluble solid from a liquid using a porous barrier?
choices: Filtration
Distillation
Chromatography
Crystallization

questions.question: Which method separates substances by boiling and condensing?
choices: Filtration
Distillation
Magnetic separation
Sieving

questions.question: What does chromatography use to separate mixture components?
choices: Differences only in particle settling under gravity
Differences only in boiling points
Different movement caused by interactions with mobile and stationary phases
Differences only in attraction to a magnet

questions.question: What is decanting?
choices: Boiling a liquid until nothing remains
Passing vapor through a magnet
Dissolving every solid in acid
Pouring off a liquid from settled solid or another liquid layer

questions.question: Which method sorts solid particles mainly by size?
choices: Sieving
Distillation
Evaporation
Solvent extraction

questions.question: What is the material left on filter paper commonly called?
choices: Filtrate
Residue
Distillate
Solvent

questions.question: Which property enables magnetic separation of iron filings from sand?
choices: Sand and iron have identical magnetic behavior
Iron always dissolves in sand
Iron is attracted strongly to a magnet
Sand has a lower atomic number than iron

questions.question: Why does ordinary filtration not remove dissolved salt from water?
choices: Dissolved ions settle immediately on the paper
Filter paper evaporates the solvent before ions pass
Filtration converts the salt into an insoluble solid
Dissolved ions pass through the filter's pores

questions.question: Why can distillation produce relatively pure water from saltwater?
choices: Water vaporizes while dissolved salt largely remains
Salt vaporizes more readily than water in ordinary distillation
Salt and water are separated only by particle diameter
Condensation removes the salt by chemical decomposition

questions.question: How can crystallization help recover a dissolved solid?
choices: Solute particles are caught while still dissolved in a filter
Reduced solubility allows solid crystals to form
Solute molecules are destroyed by lowering temperature
All solvent turns into crystals while solute remains liquid

questions.question: What is a solvent's role in solvent extraction?
choices: It magnetizes every component
It destroys all atoms in the sample
It dissolves a desired component more readily than another phase does
It necessarily has a lower density than water

questions.question: Why might fractional distillation be preferred over simple distillation for liquids with close boiling points?
choices: It sorts liquid molecules only by size through a filter
It requires both liquids to have identical vapor compositions
It works by chemically changing one liquid into another
Repeated vaporization and condensation improve separation

questions.question: Why may centrifugation speed up separation of suspended particles?
choices: Rotation accelerates settling based on particle and fluid properties
It separates dissolved ions using only a paper barrier
It increases particle solubility until all material dissolves
It makes every suspended particle the same density

questions.question: How do separating mixtures and chemically decomposing compounds differ?
choices: Mixture separation must create new elements
Mixture separation can preserve substances' chemical identities
Chemical decomposition only sorts particles by size
Both always require nuclear reactions

questions.question: Why should a separation method be chosen using mixture properties?
choices: One method separates every possible mixture equally
Only the mixture's color matters
Different methods rely on different physical differences
Physical properties do not affect separation

questions.question: A mixture contains sand and dissolved salt in water. Which sequence can recover the sand and then salt?
choices: Evaporate, then magnetize the remaining material
Filter twice with the same paper
Decant, then sieve the water
Filter, then evaporate water from the filtrate

questions.question: A mixture contains iron filings and nonmagnetic plastic beads of similar size. Which method is suitable?
choices: Use a magnet
Use a sieve with equal-size openings
Allow both solids to boil
Distill the mixture without a liquid

questions.question: Two pigments travel different distances on chromatography paper. What does this indicate?
choices: They necessarily contain different elements
They interact differently with the solvent and paper
One pigment has no molecules
Both pigments are the same pure substance

questions.question: An insoluble solid settles beneath water. Which simple method can remove most of the water without filtering?
choices: Fractional distillation of the solid
Paper chromatography of the container
Careful decanting
Magnetic separation of water

questions.question: A solution contains a dissolved substance whose solubility falls greatly when cooled. Which method can recover it as a solid?
choices: Filter the hot solution to catch dissolved particles
Use a magnet regardless of the substance
Sieve the dissolved substance directly
Cool the solution to form crystals
